subject: Temporary measurement-window adjustment & p95 allowance for hosted API
messages:
From: Kate Miller <kate@fintech-demo.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+sla@fintech-demo.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Request: hosted API p95 window for year-end batch

Hi Monica / Karthik,

Quick note from our ops team: we run a concentrated reconciliation job on Dec 20–22 between 13:00–15:00 UTC that produces a short, very high QPS spike for embeddings + generation endpoints. We've attached a traffic histogram and sample traces. During that window our observed p95 climbs dramatically for short bursts and is causing a few downstream timeouts.

We know Redwood's standard hosted SLOs are expressed as rolling p50/p95 measured over the 24h window. For this event we need either: (a) a temporary measurement-window change so the spike doesn't permanently affect our rolling SLO, or (b) an explicit short-duration p95 allowance (a formal exception) so we aren't escalated for SLA breaches.

Can you advise what options you can offer and what approvals are required? We may need formal language for procurement/legal as well.

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Miller
VP Engineering, FinTech Demo

Attachments: fintech-demo-traffic-analysis-dec2026.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Miller <kate@fintech-demo.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, ops+sla@fintech-demo.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 17:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API p95 window for year-end batch

Hi Kate — thanks for the data, that histogram is helpful. I discussed with runtime and reliability: here are two practical paths we can take and the trade-offs for procurement/legal language.

Option A — Measurement-window carve-out (preferred for short events)
- Description: For the specific event windows (Dec 20–22, 13:00–15:00 UTC) we will exclude those 2-hour blocks from the 24h rolling SLO calculation for FinTech Demo. That prevents the burst from impacting your daily rolling p95 while keeping standard SLOs intact the rest of the time.
- Mechanics: We will implement a per-account measurement filter so the metrics pipeline omits requests with the account tag during those windows.
- SLO language for addendum: "Hosted API p95 commitments will exclude designated event windows of up to 3 hours per day when mutually agreed in writing in advance."
- Impact: No customer-level credits needed if we exclude the window. Implementation requires ops/runtimes to flip a filter and a one-off PR; runtime estimates ~1–2 business days to validate.

Option B — Temporary p95 allowance (if exclusion is not acceptable)
- Description: Temporarily raise the p95 target for the specified windows to 350ms (vs. our standard 250ms) for the 3-day event window only.
- Mechanics: Applies to FinTech Demo tenant IDs during specified timestamps; will be evaluated with our standard rolling window but only within the event windows.
- SLO language: "For specified event windows, Redwood will commit to a p50 of 75ms and a p95 of 350ms measured in 5-minute rolling buckets. Failure to meet the event-window p95 may trigger proportional service credit as described in the addendum."
- Impact: Requires legal sign-off (credits are involved) and a short verification period; lower implementation complexity.

My recommendation: go with Option A (measurement exclusion) — it protects your long-term SLA without opening credit negotiation. If procurement/legal prefer explicit numbers, Option B is a straightforward addendum.

Next steps: I can prepare an SLO addendum and a DocuSign once you confirm preferred option. If you want us to proceed with the exclusion approach, we need confirmation by EOD Dec 16 so engineering can schedule the filter and testing.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

I recommended the exclusion (Option A) — less risk of ongoing credits, cleaner for our SLAs. Need quick alignment on engineering bandwidth and legal OK on statement language.

Hi Kate / Hilary — thanks for the quick review. Legal is comfortable with the measurement-window exclusion phrasing and engineering has confirmed they can implement and test the filter by Dec 19.

Confirming agreed plan:
- Scope: Dec 20–22, 2026 between 13:00–15:00 UTC (FinTech Demo tenant(s) only).
- Change: Redwood will exclude the above event windows from the rolling 24h p95 calculation for FinTech Demo.
- Limits: This exclusion will apply to up to 6 total event hours in the quarter for which prior written notice is provided.
- Timeline: engineering will stage in a canary environment on Dec 18, run validation on Dec 19, and flip the production filter on Dec 20 at 12:50 UTC.
- Documentation: I will attach the SLO addendum and send a DocuSign link for signature (see link).

Next steps for you: please confirm acceptance in reply and provide the legal contact who will sign the addendum (Hilary copied). Once we have signature we'll schedule the change and share the verification checklist.

If you prefer the explicit p95 numbers instead we can do that as a short alternative addendum; we find exclusion is less error-prone.

Best regards,
